content:
Women's suffrage was adopted at the federal level in Switzerland in **1971**.

Switzerland was one of the last Western countries to grant women the right to vote in federal elections. Women in Switzerland had previously gained the vote in some cantons (starting as early as 1959 in Vaud), but it wasn't until a referendum held on February 7, 1971, that Swiss men voted to extend federal voting rights to women nationwide. The referendum passed with approximately 66% in favor.
